newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks see modest losses by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks see modest losses by close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower in choppy trade on Tuesday, after having spent most of the day confined to an eight point trading range.
While softer metals prices ensured a shaky start to the day, the resource leaders quickly came off their lows.
Afternoon strength in the banking sector ensured the day's losses were modest.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.0 points lower at 2,380.1.
December share price index futures were six points lower at 2,386 and were at a 5.9 point premium to the index.
"The market is very strong in some stocks," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co, citing Commonwealth Bank as ANZ Bank as examples while other players echoed his sentiments.
"They (the banks) kept it together in the afternoon. National Australia Bank saw profit taking but the rest looked pretty good," said a Sydney broker.
A note of caution was sounded as to whether the softer trend in the resources stocks was likely to be reversed, with the strong Australian dollar seen as an obstacle to recovery.
"Commodities are not going to do a great deal while the Australian dollar is so high," Struk said.
Gold stocks were the biggest losers on the day, the gold index closing 1.9 percent weaker, compared to a loss in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of just 0.2 percent.

On the upside, shares in property developer and financial services group, Lend Lease, raced to record highs after announcing a deal to cede its general insurance customers to QBE Insurance, whose own shares also received a boost.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading was similar to the choppy trade seen in the underlying market. Options trade was slow.
Total options traded 30,484 (24,629)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,209 (8,162).
In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended just above the day's lows as the market got caught up in speculation of a further monetary policy easing as the RBA board met today.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.03 percent.

The Australian dollar continued its mild correction to settle lower despite a samurai-induced spike above US$0.8150 in the afternoon. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.8140/45, down from US$0.8198/03 here late Monday.
